div.head: Wi 26.1
div.ab: Se þe hine gefo ⁊ gegange, healfne hine age; gif hine man cwelle, geselle heom man LXX scll'.
Se þe hine gefo ⁊ gegange, healfne hine age; gif hine man cwelle, geselle heom man LXX scll'.
Se þe hine gefo ⁊ gegange, healfne hine age. Gif hine man cwelle, geselle heom man LXX scƚƚ.
Der welcher ihn fasst und stellt, besitze ihn zur Hälfte; wenn man jenen tödtet, so gebe man ihm [dem Einfänger] 70 Schll.
The one who seizes and holds him is to have half of him; if he is killed, let [the captor] be given 70 shillings.
He who catches and secures him, shall have half his value. If he is put to death, 70 shillings shall be paid to him.
He who discovers and captures him, is to have the right to half of [the payment for] him; if he is killed, 70 shillings is to be paid to them.
He who seizes and delivers him [the thief], owns him half; if he [the thief] is killed, let them be paid 70 shillings.

note.seg: Auch o. 11 teilt der Ankläger den Ertrag aus Strafprozess mit dem Richter zur Hälfte. Er erhält ¹/₂ vom Preis für den Verknechteten oder vom Wergeld
Above 11, too, the accuser shares the proceeds of the criminal proceedings half and half with the judge. He receives ¹/₂ of the price for the man enslaved or of the wergild
Der Richter zahlt aus des Diebes Habe, den mit dem Tode auch Vermögenseinziehung traf, den Ersatz an den Bestohlenen und Fängerlohn an den Anzeiger
Out of the property of the thief, who together with death also suffered confiscation of his property, the judge pays the restitution to the person robbed and the captor’s reward to the informer
Wenn die hoch scheinende Summe richtig (nicht etwa aus 27 verderbt) ist, bedeutet sie Lohn der Polizei (s. d. Gl 1 E) für Einfang des Verbrechers
If the sum, which seems high, is correct (and not, say, corrupted from 27), it represents a reward for police action (see that word in Gl 1 E) in capturing the criminal
The sum (70 shillings) specified here and in cap. 27 seems hardly credible, but it is not easy to suggest what the right sum should be.

note.label: them
note.seg: His capturers, who would otherwise lose by the king’s choice of the death-penalty. But if heom is a mistake for the singular, him, it could mean “for him” and the situation envisaged might be if the capturer took the law into his own hands, killed the thief, and thus robbed the king of his choice. He would have to compensate for it.

note.label: half;
note.seg: Presumably half the value of the stolen goods. From Æbt §15, we know that the original owner was recompensed three-fold. Conceivably half of the total fine goes to the captor. It is possible that this might either mean half the thief’s possessions or half his labour as an esne, although in the latter case one might expect the time period to be stipulated.

note.label: shillings.
note.seg: ‘His capturers, who would otherwise lose by the king’s choice of the death-penalty. But if heom is a mistake for the singular him, it could mean “for him” and the situation envisaged might be if the capturer took the law into his own hands, killed the thief, and thus robbed the king of his choice. He would have to compensate for it.’ See Whitelock, English Historical Documents, 398.
